title: SHAKTI: Securing Hardware IPs by Cascade Gated Multiplexer-Based Logic Obfuscation
problem: Logic locking vulnerable to SAT/structural learning attacks; MUX-based locking susceptible despite effectiveness
motivation: Distributed chip design chain faces IP piracy/overproduction; logic locking essential; need attack-resilient locking
method: SHAKTI protects hardware by inserting cascaded gated multiplexers (logic gates that route signals differently based on a secret key) connected in a daisy-chain, where each gate's output feeds the next. The entire chain is controlled by a 64-128 bit secret key. Because each gate depends on the previous gate's output, cracking one gate doesn't reveal the complete key—an attacker would need to understand how all the gates work together.
key_novelty: Linking gated multiplexers in a daisy-chain—where each logic gate routes signals based on a secret key and feeds the next—creates a hardware lock resistant to SAT solver and structural learning attacks, with only 19.32-19.45% additional chip area.
contributions: SAT attack timeout on all netlists
